reviewScope: Unblinded manual review of all twenty actual brief/detailed causal followups, each with identical explicit frozen context. Exact text replay with a signed-in backend; neither native ASR nor independent expert certification. Objectives run sequentially; provider drift remains possible.

measurements.scope: Observed fixture workload; sample p95 is not a population guarantee. Missing/incorrect/incomplete rows remain in counts and have no successful latency. HTTP actual wire write remains unknown when not instrumented.
measurements.nonFaultNonObserverScope: Excludes requested transport-fault probes and disclosed observer interference. All rows remain in correctness/completion/missing counts and overall latency distributions. This exclusion alone does not certify a healthy warm path.
measurements.nonFaultProbeScope: Excludes requested transport-fault probes, including unsupported or unconfirmed injections. Does not independently certify every remaining sample as a healthy warm connection.

allFollowupUsefulP95Ms.scope: Missing, incorrect and unverified useful delivery rank after finite correct delivery; missing latency is never replaced with a timeout value.

panelTransitions.scope: Sampled viewport transitions and native/host clock bounds. Upper bounds allow prior text until the first observed clearing/new-generation paint; an unobserved blank paint may make the actual interval shorter. Lower bounds use only observed old-generation paint after acceptance. Not a universal stale-output certificate.

rows.name: detailed-why-1
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because the GPU schedules a warp of 32 threads together, issuing a common instruction to its active lanes rather than independently issuing instructions for every thread. If threads take different branches, each branch’s instructions run with only the lanes that chose it active; the other lanes are masked off. This shared execution machinery makes GPUs efficient, but divergent branches can reduce throughput.

review.note: Common issue instead of independent per-thread issue explains masked paths and the efficiency tradeoff.
review.usefulPrefix: Because the GPU schedules a warp of 32 threads together, issuing a common instruction to its active lanes rather than independently issuing instructions for every thread.

rows.name: detailed-why-2
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares instruction issue: the GPU executes an instruction across its active threads together, rather than giving each thread a fully independent instruction stream. If threads take different branches, it executes the required paths with masks that enable only the threads belonging to each path. That’s why divergence can reduce efficiency: some lanes are inactive while the other branch runs.

review.note: Shared issue, path masks and inactive lanes explain divergence cost.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares instruction issue: the GPU executes an instruction across its active threads together, rather than giving each thread a fully independent instruction stream.

rows.name: detailed-why-3
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares instruction issue: the GPU issues the same instruction to its 32 thread lanes, each operating on its own data. If threads take different branches, the GPU executes each needed path with only that path’s lanes active, masking out the others. That’s called branch divergence, and it can reduce throughput because some lanes sit idle.

review.note: Shared instruction across own data, masked branch paths and idle lanes give the mechanism.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares instruction issue: the GPU issues the same instruction to its 32 thread lanes, each operating on its own data.

rows.name: detailed-why-4
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because the threads in a warp share instruction-issue hardware, rather than each having a fully independent execution engine. A CUDA warp groups 32 threads, and an issued instruction runs on the active lanes. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes each needed path with nonparticipating lanes disabled, so divergence can reduce throughput.

review.note: Shared issue hardware rather than fully independent engines explains participation masks.
review.usefulPrefix: Because the threads in a warp share instruction-issue hardware, rather than each having a fully independent execution engine.

rows.name: detailed-why-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a CUDA warp shares instruction issue across 32 threads, rather than each thread independently issuing instructions. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes the required paths with an active-lane mask, so only the threads belonging to each path do work. This is called warp divergence, and it can reduce efficiency because some lanes are inactive while another path runs.

review.note: Shared issue and active mask explain lost useful work, not merely a definition.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a CUDA warp shares instruction issue across 32 threads, rather than each thread independently issuing instructions.

rows.name: detailed-why-6
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes the needed paths with an active-lane mask, so only the threads belonging to each path do work. That’s why divergence can reduce efficiency: some lanes sit idle while another path runs.

review.note: Shared instruction stream and idle lanes provide the causal explanation.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data.

rows.name: detailed-why-7
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads, rather than each thread independently issuing instructions. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes the required paths with an active-lane mask, so only the threads belonging to each path do work. This is called branch divergence, and it can reduce efficiency because some lanes are inactive during each path.

review.note: Shared stream and path masks explain inactive lanes and reduced efficiency.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads, rather than each thread independently issuing instructions.

rows.name: detailed-why-8
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data. When threads choose different branches, the GPU runs each required path with an active-lane mask, so only the threads that chose that path perform its work. That’s why branch divergence can reduce efficiency: some lanes are inactive while another path runs.

review.note: Shared stream and path masks give a causal rather than definitional answer.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data.

rows.name: detailed-why-9
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads, rather than giving each thread fully independent instruction execution. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes each required path with only its matching lanes active, masking out the others. That’s called branch divergence, and it reduces efficiency because fewer lanes do useful work during each path.

review.note: Shared stream rather than independent execution explains masked path participation and cost.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a CUDA warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads, rather than giving each thread fully independent instruction execution.

rows.name: detailed-why-10
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data. When threads take different branches, the GPU masks off lanes that don’t belong to the path currently executing, then executes the other path for its lanes. That’s branch divergence, and it can reduce efficiency because fewer lanes do useful work during each path.

review.note: Shared stream and separately masked needed paths explain lost useful parallel work.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: its 32 threads normally execute the same instruction on different data.
